m: Salutation to Shri Ganesha. Om. Of this Shri Kunjika hymn-mantra, the seer is Sadashiva, the metre is anushtubh, the deity is she whose self is the three qualities, the seed is Om Aim, the power is Om Hrim, and the pin is Om Klim. This direction is for recitation in order to fulfill all that I seek. Shiva said: Listen, Goddess. I will declare the excellent Kunjika hymn, by whose mantra-power the recitation of Chandi becomes auspicious.
There is no kavacha, no Argala hymn, no Kilaka, no secret text, no hymn of praise, no meditation, no nyasa, and no separate worship.
By the mere recitation of the Kunjika one obtains the fruit of reciting the Durga text. It is exceedingly secret, Goddess, and hard for even the gods to obtain.

It should be guarded with effort, Parvati, as one guards one's own source. Slaying, bewildering, bringing under one's will, stopping, driving away, and the rest succeed by the mere recitation of this excellent Kunjika hymn.

Then the mantra. Om Aim Hrim Klim Chamundayai Vichche. Om glaum hum klim jum sah: blaze, blaze, burn, burn, blaze forth, blaze forth. Aim Hrim Klim Chamundayai Vichche. Burn. Ham sam lam ksham phat svaha.

Thus the mantra. Hrim hrim klim: cause to flow, cause to flow; destroy the curse, destroy it. Shrim shrim shrim jum sah: cause to flow. Adaya svaha. Om shlim hum klim glam jum sah: burn, blaze up, blaze the mantra forth. Ham sam lam ksham phat svaha. Salutation to you whose form is Rudra. Salutation to you, crusher of Madhu. Salutation to you, slayer of Kaitabha. Salutation to you, crusher of Mahisha.
Salutation to you, slayer of Shumbha, and to you, striker of the asura Nishumbha. Be awake, great Goddess, and make my recitation successful.
Salutation to you in the form of the seed: to the form of creation in Aim, to the protector in Hrim, and to her whose form is desire in Klim.
Chamunda is the slayer of Chanda. The syllable ai grants the boon. Vichche always gives fearlessness. Salutation to you, whose form is the mantra.
Dham dhim dhum, wife of the matted-haired one. Vam vim vum, sovereign of speech. Kram krim krum, Goddess Kunjika. Sham shim shum, make what is auspicious for me.
Hum hum, to her whose form is the humkara. Jam jam jam, she who devours and the rest. Bhram bhrim bhrum, Bhairavi. Salutation and salutation to you, gracious Bhavani.
Am kam cham tam tam pam yam sham vim dum aim vim ham ksham. Awaken the knowledge, awaken the knowledge. Break, break. Make it blazing, make it blazing. Svaha.

Hrim ksham kshim srim: enliven, enliven; break, break; devour, devour; kindle, kindle; release, release. Hum phat jram vaushat. Aim hrim klim: colour, colour; cause to cling, cause to cling; sound, sound; bind, bind. Bhram bhrim bhrum, Bhairavi, gracious one: contract, contract; break, break. Mlim svaha.

Pam pim pum, Parvati, the complete one. Kham khim khum, and the sky-goer. Mlam mlim mlum, widely extended at the root, for the sake of the Kunjika hymn. Sam sim sum, Goddess of the Saptashati, accomplish for me the success of the mantra.
Salutation and salutation to the Kunjika. This Kunjika hymn is for the sake of awakening the mantra. It should not be given to one without devotion. Guard it as a secret, Parvati.

Whoever recites the Saptashati without the Kunjika, Goddess, does not obtain success, as a cry in the forest does not. Thus the Kunjika hymn in the conversation of Shiva and Parvati, in the Gauri Tantra of the Shri Rudra Yamala, is complete. Thus the Kunjika hymn in the conversation of Ishvara and Parvati, in the Shri Damara Tantra, is complete.
